items.title: Show HN: Inference Cooperative, user-governed AI
items.desc: description: A membergoverned cooperative for AI inference. Direct the models, the values, and the direction — together. title: Inference Cooperative — AI, governed together image: https://inference.coop/inferencecard.png Inference Cooperative inference.coop AI, governed together. We don't have to accept the choices Big Tech gives us. We can make our own. Membergoverned Open source Privacy options Renewable options [Become a member](https://opencollective.com/inferencecooperative/contribute/sponsors105477/checkout?interval=month&amount=5) [Member login](https://my.inference.coop) AI is becoming infrastructure. The models shaping how we work, learn, and talk are owned by a handful of companies — and governed first for their shareholders' profit. We think that's backwards. A tool this consequential should answer to the people who use it. So we're enabling access to AI on the users' terms. One membership. A fair price, a full seat. Everyone joins the same way, and everyone gets the same things — the difference is what you can afford to give, not what you get back. Pay what's fair Dues are a sliding scale starting at $5 a month — you choose the amount that fits your circumstances. (Many members pay $15.) Everyone gets the same allowance Today, every member gets a $15 monthly credit for chat and API alike, whether you pay $5 or $20. Need more? Add credits When the allowance isn't enough, buy a credit pack. Credits never expire, carry over month to month, and kick in only after your allowance is used. Chat, API, and a vote One membership opens the chat, the developer API, and a seat in governance. Leave any time Cancel whenever you like. Your data stays yours. Pricing is itself a coop decision. As usage grows, the current scale will need to change — and members will decide how, together. Choose by what you value. Different members care about different things. So we let you choose your AI by the values that matter to you — not lock you to a single provider. Privacy Models running in encrypted enclaves, so even we can't read your prompts or responses. Renewable energy Models served on 100% renewable power, for members who want their AI to be lighter on the planet. Publicly developed Open, sovereign models built as public goods rather than proprietary products. The exact lineup changes as the coop decides. Chat Your own chat, tuned to the value you pick. Web search built in File uploads & documents Pick the model and provider each time Developer API Bring your own tools, through a standard endpoint. OpenAIcompatible Your own API keys Shares the same monthly allowance Help run the AI you use. Join the cooperative, and help decide where it goes next. [Become a member](https://opencollective.com/inferencecooperative/contribute/sponsors105477/checkout?interval=month&amount=5) [Read the docs](https://git.inference.coop/coop/docs) json { "@context": "https://schema.org", "@type": "Organization", "name": "Inference Cooperative", "url": "https://inference.coop/", "email": "info@inference.coop", "description": "A membergoverned cooperative for AI inference. Direct the models, the values, and the direction — together." }
items.author: ntnsndr
items.descZh: Inference Cooperative 是一个颠覆性的由会员共同治理的 AI 推理合作社，旨在打破少数科技巨头对 AI 基础设施的垄断，让模型、价值观和发展方向由使用者共同决定。其核心机制是普惠式的会员制，月费采用滑动标准起步价仅为 5 美元（多数会员支付 15 美元），每位会员每月均可获得 15 美元的等额聊天与 API 额度，未用完的积分可无限期跨月结转。平台的突出亮点在于将选择权交还给用户，提供基于加密 enclave 的绝对隐私模型、100% 可再生能源运行的绿色 AI，以及作为公共产品开发的开源主权模型。此外，它提供 OpenAI 兼容的开发者 API、内置网页搜索及文件上传功能，支持用户自带密钥，确保了技术工具的自主性。这一模式特别适用于追求数据隐私、注重环保、希望摆脱大厂锁定并深度参与 AI 治理的个人开发者与企业。
items.quote: 一个如此重要的工具，应当对使用者负责。

items.title: Show HN: CallFlow – VS Code REST client that also captures your terminal's HTTP
items.desc: description: A REST client for VS Code, Cursor and VSCodium that keeps requests as plain .http files, plus a Pro HTTP debugger that captures your workspace traffic locally. No account, and your requests never leave your machine. [Skip to content](main) Your API requests belong in files you own, next to your code. Seeing what that code actually sends should not need an account or a server. CallFlow is a VS Code extension. The free REST client keeps every request as a plain .http file in your workspace — it diffs in git and opens in REST Client if we ever disappear. Pro adds an HTTP debugger: start capture, and every terminal and debug session in the workspace routes through a local proxy on your machine, so you can inspect, save, replay and export the calls your code really made. [Get CallFlow — Free](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=smallhours.callflow) [Buy Pro — $20 once]() Pro free for 14 days in the editor, no account. Buying for a team? [Company licence, $49 per seat →](teams) VS Code 1.90+ · Cursor and VSCodium, tested · No account. Your requests stay on your machine. [How it works →](howitworks) How it actually works Not marketing language — this is the literal request and capture path, because a "local only" promise is only as good as its mechanism. 1. A request is a .http file, and nothing else Collections are folders under .callflow/ in your workspace. Each file holds one or more requests separated by , in the same format REST Client has read since 2016: method and URL, headers, a blank line, the body. There is no database, no proprietary bundle, and nothing that stops working if you uninstall the extension. The files diff in git like any other source. 2. Environments keep secrets out of the file environments.json holds your variables per environment. Any variable you list under secretsis stored in VS Code's SecretStorage instead — the file on disk keeps an empty string, so a token never ends up in a commit. Variables resolve filefirst, then environment, then dynamic values like {{$uuid}}, then chained values from an earlier response. 3. Sending uses Node's own HTTP stack, so timings are real Requests go out over node:http and node:https directly, not fetch, which is what makes DNS, connect, TLS and firstbyte timings precise and cancellation immediate. Redirects are followed up to ten times and the Authorization header is never forwarded to a different origin. 4. Capture (Pro) is a proxy on 127.0.0.1, scoped to your workspace Start capture and CallFlow opens a proxy on a random port bound to 127.0.0.1 only. It then sets HTTP_PROXY, HTTPS_PROXY and the CAbundle variables that Node, Python, curl, Git, the AWS SDK, Deno, Cargo and Java honour — in this workspace's terminals and debug sessions, through VS Code's own environment mechanism. No system proxy setting is touched, nothing outside VS Code is routed, and stopping capture clears it all. 5. The certificate authority is generated on your machine To read HTTPS, CallFlow generates a local CA on first use and keeps the private key in VS Code's storage with owneronly permissions. For terminal targets you do not need to trust it systemwide, because the environment variables point each tool at the CA file directly. System trust only matters for GUI apps, and the exact command is shown before it runs, never behind a silent prompt. Secrets are masked before they reach the screen Captured traffic and history can contain the very things you would not want on a screenshot. Values of Authorization, Cookie, SetCookie and XAPIKey are masked in the inspector and in HAR export by default (the list is a setting), and you reveal them deliberately, per view. Bodies are stored only in your own VS Code storage and are never synced. Pro licences don't phone home either A CallFlow Pro licence is a small signed key that the extension checks entirely on its own, offline, using publickey verification. It never contacts a server to validate a purchase — not at activation, not afterward. That's a deliberate trade: we can't detect a copied key, and we would rather not have the extension report on how your licence is used. The only thing CallFlow sends on its own is an anonymous onceaday "this install is in use" ping with no licence details in it (see [Privacy](trust)). Free vs Pro Free is the complete REST client, forever. Pro is the HTTP debugger on top of it — never access to your own files. __Feature comparison between CallFlow Free and CallFlow Pro__ Feature Free Pro Request editor & response viewer Included Included Collections as plain .http files in your workspace Included Included Environments, variables & auth helpers Included Included Import from cURL, Thunder Client, Postman v2.1 & HAR Included Included Export your requests, history & captures (cURL, HAR) Included, forever Included, forever Request history 200 entries 20,000 entries Capture traffic from terminals & debug sessions — Included Inspect captured requests & responses — Included Save a captured call as a request — Included Replay & editreplay — Included Collection runner: run a folder, chain values, see what failed Included Included Scripts & tests (sandboxed), datadriven runs, JUnit export — Included Response diff — Included Price $0 $20 onetime[$49/seat for teams](teams) [Buy CallFlow Pro — $20]() Onetime. Sold through Paddle. Key shown on screen after payment. Or try every Pro feature free for 14 days in the editor first: no account. Buying for a team? See the [company licence](teams) just below. For teams: $49 per seat A company licence lets your employer buy CallFlow Pro for everyone who needs it, with one invoice. Same Pro, same offline keys, no accounts and no seattracking server: everyone on the team enters the same key and that's it. Seats [Buy company licence]() $49 per seat, onetime. One key for the whole team. Tax invoice from Paddle, our reseller. Need a quote for procurement? Email [hello@smallhours.works](mailto:hello@smallhours.works?subject=CallFlow
items.author: arexey
items.descZh: CallFlow是一个针对VS Code、Cursor和VSCodium的REST客户端扩展，其核心理念是将API请求以纯文本.http文件形式存储在用户工作区中，确保数据完全本地化，无需账户或外部服务器。免费版提供了完整的REST客户端功能，包括请求编辑、响应查看、集合管理和环境变量支持，所有数据以文件形式存在，便于版本控制。Pro版在此基础上增加了HTTP调试器，通过本地代理捕获工作区内所有终端和调试会话的流量，支持检查、保存、重放和导出，其中请求历史容量从免费版的200条提升至20,000条。亮点包括使用Node的HTTP栈实现精确的DNS、连接、TLS和首字节计时，以及离线许可证验证机制，确保无服务器通信。适用场景主要是开发者在VS Code中需要高效管理API请求并深度调试HTTP流量的场景，特别适合注重隐私和本地控制的团队。
items.quote: 您的 API 请求应放在您自己的文件中，与您的代码放在一起。

items.author: josefchen
items.descZh: RoboJev 解决了机器人领域数据爆炸但人工标注任务成功与否极其耗时的痛点。其核心功能是利用 AI 自动评估机器人视频，声称比人工生成数据更快。亮点在于性能极其出色，相比 6 Astra 方案便宜 48 倍且快 28 倍，同时拥有 27B 参数并开源权重。具体测试中，它能在仅花费 13.16 美元 GPU 时间的情况下完成对 68,555 个 episode（501 小时视频）的评估，而同类方案需 637 美元。该产品适用于需要高效、低成本评估机器人任务表现的研究与开发场景。
items.quote: RoboJev：人们正在观看数千个视频来标注任务是否成功。现在，你可以比生成数据更快地为机器人数据打分。
items.titleZh: Show HN：与 6 Astra 相比，27B 开放模型可对机器人数据进行评分，价格便宜 48 倍/速度快 27 倍

it fits together, not as a flat list of diffs. When a coding agent writes most of the code, reviewing it means opening the changed files in your IDE one by one and rebuilding in your head what calls what, which path a request now takes, and which test covers which piece. The diff shows lines; the structure of the change is left for you to work out. taskview puts that structure on the page for you. When the agent finishes a task, it describes its change: the functions, components and tests it touched, why, how they relate, and the uservisible flows they form. taskview turns that into one page you read in the browser: a graph of the change, its flows step by step, and each piece's code next to the agent's reason for it. You spend your attention judging the code, not reconstructing it. [](/gtindo/taskview/blob/main/docs/images/graph.png) What you get The relations, already drawn. Changed functions, components, endpoints and tests as a graph, across repos, so you see what connects to what without holding it in your head. Flows, step by step. Each path through the change from entry point to boundary, with the tests that exercise it attached to the steps they cover. Code in context. Click any piece to read its diff, or the code as it reads after the change, next to why the agent changed it and what it relates to. A map you can trust. Every file, line and commit the agent points at is checked against Git, and the diff map flags changed lines the agent didn't describe, so the map matches the real diff. Whether the code is right is still your call: test results and explanations are shown as the agent's word. One offline HTML file per task that you can keep or share. Building it only reads files and runs readonly Git; it never runs your tests, builds or other tooling. Works with any programming language. Nothing is parsed: the map is built from files, line ranges and diffs, so it fits Go, TypeScript, Python, Rust, SQL, config or infrastructure code alike, and changes that span several languages and repos (a web client and its API, say). Syntax highlighting covers about 300 languages; anything else shows as plain text. Works with any coding agent that can follow written instructions: Claude Code, Codex, and others. Install taskview installs for your user only: no sudo or administrator rights. The only runtime dependency is git. macOS and Linux: curl fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gtindo/taskview/main/scripts/install.sh sh Windows (PowerShell): irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gtindo/taskview/main/scripts/instal

[go.sum](/soollabs/holdmydocs/blob/main/go.sum "go.sum") View all files Repository files navigation Hold My Docs A wiki that gets on with it. Hold My Docs (HMD) runs as a single Go binary and keeps your content as Markdown in an ordinary Git repository. Every save is a commit, so your docs have real history and can sync to a remote you already use. [](/soollabs/holdmydocs/blob/main/docs/hero.png) Warning Hold My Docs is an earlystage project. Expect rough edges and breaking changes. Keep backups and test upgrades before relying on it as your only source for important documentation. [](/soollabs/holdmydocs/blob/main/docs/demo.webp) Features Every save is a Git commit, and the wiki can push to and pull from a remote you configure. Readonly mode clones a public docs repository without a Git token, so you can browse it and pull updates. Namespaces give each area of the wiki its own visibility, navigation, appearance and pagecreation defaults. The Markdown editor has a preview, wikilinks, backlinks, Mermaid diagrams, attachments, history and revert, and fulltext search covers every page. With an operatorsupplied Apache Tika Server, HMD also searches PDF and Office attachments locally, combining keyword and semantic search. People sign in with local accounts or OIDC single signon; access scopes and personal access tokens limit what each user or tool can do. An MCP server lets authorised agents read and write ordinary pages, with optional attachment search limited to chosen namespaces. Static export publishes a namespace as a site that runs without HMD. Quick start Docker Compose export HMD_ADMIN_USER=admin export HMD_ADMIN_PASSWORD='useauniquepasswordofatleast12characters' docker compose up d curl f http://127.0.0.1:8080/_/ready Open <http://localhost:8080 and sign in with the bootstrap credentials. Remove the bootstrap environment variables after the first successful start. The Compose file starts a localonly instance bound to loopback. To sync to a Git remote, create ./git_token.txt and uncomment the HMD_GIT_ variables and the git_token secret. For document search, uncomment HMD_DOCUMENT_SEARCH_TIKA_URL and run with docker compose profile documents up. Keep Tika private; see the docs site for hardening and sandboxing. Bare binary go build o hmd ./cmd/hmd HMD_SERVER_BIND=:8080 \ HMD_SERVER_REPO_DIR=./data/repo \ HMD_APP_DIR=./data/app \ HMD_ADMIN_USER=admin HMD_ADMIN_PASSWORD='useauniquepasswordofatleast12characters' \ ./hmd Keep HMD_APP_DIR on local disk (not NFS); HMD_SERVER_REPO_DIR can be on network storage. Documentation The [HMD docs site](https://hmd.sool.dev) covers installation, configuration, operations, MCP, and development. AI use Parts of HMD are developed with AI coding assistants and several models. The maintainer reviews, corrects, and tests all changes and is responsible for the result. License MIT.
